topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under WV Code §30-40-7(a), in what capacity may the West Virginia Real Estate Commission sue and be sued?
choice_a: As an agency of the state, in its official name
choice_b: As a private corporation
choice_c: Only through the Attorney General
choice_d: It may not be sued
explanation: §30-40-7(a) expressly grants the commission authority to sue and be sued in its official name as an agency of the state, giving it independent legal capacity to enforce and defend its actions under the licensing article.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Who does the West Virginia Real Estate Commission employ to manage its day-to-day administrative operations, per §30-40-7(b)?
choice_a: A chief financial officer
choice_b: An executive director, whose compensation the commission fixes
choice_c: The Governor's designee
choice_d: A rotating chairperson
explanation: §30-40-7(b) requires the commission to employ an executive director and fix that person's compensation, subject to general state law, and to determine the executive director's duties as necessary to carry out the article.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Besides an executive director, §30-40-7(c) authorizes the commission to employ or contract with which of the following as necessary?
choice_a: Only licensed real estate appraisers
choice_b: County sheriffs
choice_c: Investigators, hearing examiners, attorneys, consultants, clerks, and assistants
choice_d: Only outside legal counsel
explanation: §30-40-7(c) allows the commission to employ or contract with investigators, hearing examiners, attorneys, consultants, clerks, and assistants as it deems necessary, and to fix their duties and compensation subject to general state law.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Which of the following may issue subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum on behalf of the West Virginia Real Estate Commission under §30-40-7(d)?
choice_a: Only a circuit court judge
choice_b: Only the Attorney General
choice_c: Only the full commission voting unanimously
choice_d: Any member, the executive director, or a duly authorized representative
explanation: §30-40-7(d) gives the commission authority to issue subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum through any member, its executive director, or any duly authorized representative, supporting its investigative and hearing functions.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-7(g), the commission may enter into agreements with other jurisdictions for what purpose?
choice_a: To recognize another jurisdiction's license as qualifying a nonresident for a WV license (reciprocity)
choice_b: To transfer disciplinary authority to another state
choice_c: To share fee revenue
choice_d: To jointly administer the WV exam only
explanation: §30-40-7(g) permits the commission to enter agreements with other jurisdictions whereby a license issued elsewhere may be recognized as successfully qualifying a nonresident applicant for a West Virginia license.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: How often must the West Virginia Real Estate Commission meet, at minimum, under §30-40-7(m)?
choice_a: Once each fiscal quarter
choice_b: Once each calendar year
choice_c: Twice each calendar year
choice_d: Only when a complaint is pending
explanation: §30-40-7(m) requires the commission to meet at least once each calendar year at a place and time it designates, and at such other times and places as it considers necessary to conduct commission business.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: What publication does §30-40-7(n) require the commission to produce?
choice_a: A quarterly newsletter
choice_b: A market conditions report
choice_c: An annual directory of licensees
choice_d: A continuing-education catalog
explanation: §30-40-7(n) requires the commission to publish an annual directory of licensees, in compliance with the general publication requirement found in §30-1-13.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-7(o), the commission may sponsor real estate-related educational seminars, courses, workshops, or institutes and may:
choice_a: Never charge attendees
choice_b: Only offer them free to licensees under discipline
choice_c: Delegate this entirely to private vendors with no commission involvement
choice_d: Charge a fee for attendance and incur/pay necessary expenses
explanation: §30-40-7(o) authorizes the commission to sponsor educational seminars, courses, workshops, or institutes, incur and pay necessary expenses, and charge a fee for attendance.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: §30-40-7(r) authorizes the commission to provide which type of educational option for license applicants?
choice_a: Distance education courses sufficient to meet prelicense educational requirements
choice_b: In-person seminars only
choice_c: College credit courses only
choice_d: Mandatory apprenticeships
explanation: §30-40-7(r) allows the commission to provide distance education courses for license applicants sufficient to meet the prelicense educational requirements in §30-40-14(a) and (b).

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: §30-40-7(s) contains a broad catch-all provision. What does it authorize the commission to do?
choice_a: Amend the statute itself without legislative approval
choice_b: Take all other actions necessary and proper to effectuate the purposes of the article
choice_c: Waive any licensing requirement at its discretion
choice_d: Delegate all its powers to the executive director
explanation: §30-40-7(s) closes the list of enumerated powers with a general catch-all: the commission shall take all other actions necessary and proper to effectuate the purposes of Article 40.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-8(a), how must the commission's proposed legislative rules be adopted?
choice_a: By unilateral commission vote with no outside review
choice_b: By referendum of licensees
choice_c: In accordance with Article 3, Chapter 29A of the WV Code (the State Administrative Procedures Act), subject to legislative approval
choice_d: By executive order of the Governor alone
explanation: §30-40-8(a) requires the commission to propose rules for legislative approval in accordance with Article 3, Chapter 29A of the WV Code, the State Administrative Procedures Act, covering everything from fees to professional conduct standards.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-8(a)(1), fees the commission establishes by rule for applications, examinations, licenses, and similar purposes are subject to what restriction?
choice_a: They must be prorated for partial years
choice_b: They must be refunded if an applicant fails the exam
choice_c: They may only be set by the Legislature directly
choice_d: None may be prorated or refunded
explanation: §30-40-8(a)(1) provides that fees for applications, examinations, licenses, renewals, license changes, courses, investigations, records copies, certifications, and other necessary fees are none of them prorated or refundable.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Which of the following is an area the commission may regulate by rule under §30-40-8(a)(11)?
choice_a: The form and use of contracts used in a real estate transaction
choice_b: State income tax rates
choice_c: Zoning ordinances
choice_d: Property tax assessments
explanation: §30-40-8(a)(11) lists the form and use of contracts used in a real estate transaction among the subjects the commission may address through its rule-making authority.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: §30-40-8(a)(13) gives the commission rule-making authority over which subject?
choice_a: Federal fair housing enforcement
choice_b: Professional conduct requirements for licensees
choice_c: Municipal business licensing
choice_d: State court procedure
explanation: §30-40-8(a)(13) authorizes the commission to establish professional conduct requirements for licensees through legislative rule.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-7(q), the commission's compliance-audit authority extends to which of the following?
choice_a: Only licensed brokers
choice_b: Only unlicensed persons suspected of practicing without a license
choice_c: Real estate brokerage offices, education providers, or any other person regulated by the commission
choice_d: Only entities that have previously been disciplined
explanation: §30-40-7(q) authorizes the commission to perform compliance audits on real estate brokerage offices, education providers, or any other person regulated by the commission, a broader reach than brokers alone.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-7(k), when may the commission examine the books and records relating to a licensee's real estate business?
choice_a: At any time, for any reason, without notice
choice_b: Only after a criminal conviction
choice_c: Only during the renewal application period
choice_d: Only if the licensee is charged in a complaint alleging a violation of the article, a commission rule, or a commission order/final decision
explanation: §30-40-7(k) permits the commission to examine a licensee's business books and records only if the licensee is charged in a complaint alleging a violation of the article, a commission rule, or a commission order or final decision.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-7(k), once a books-and-records examination is triggered by a pending complaint, how far may that examination extend?
choice_a: It may not extend beyond the specific violation charged in the complaint
choice_b: It may cover the licensee's entire career
choice_c: It may extend to any other licensee at the same brokerage
choice_d: It has no limitation once initiated
explanation: §30-40-7(k) expressly provides that such an examination 'shall not extend beyond the specific violation charged in the complaint,' limiting the scope of the commission's complaint-driven review of records.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: How are the commission's audit, investigation, and enforcement activities under Article 40 primarily funded, per §30-40-9?
choice_a: Through direct General Revenue Fund appropriations
choice_b: Through the "real estate license fund," a special revenue fund into which license fees are deposited, with no charge against the General Revenue Fund
choice_c: Through federal HUD grants exclusively
choice_d: Through mandatory annual assessments on the public
explanation: §30-40-9(a)-(b) directs fees and other moneys (except administrative fines) into the special revenue "real estate license fund," which the commission retains and uses only for administering and enforcing the article, with no compensation or expense charged against the General Revenue Fund.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Which statement best distinguishes the two audit-related powers found in §30-40-7?
choice_a: Both subsections authorize identical unlimited audits
choice_b: Neither subsection allows examination of records without a court order
choice_c: Subsection (q) allows broad compliance audits of brokerage offices, education providers, or other regulated persons, while subsection (k) allows a narrower book examination tied to and limited by a specific pending complaint
choice_d: Subsection (k) is broader than subsection (q)
explanation: Subsection (q) is a general, proactive compliance-audit power over brokerage offices, education providers, and other regulated persons, whereas subsection (k) is a narrower, complaint-triggered examination of a specific licensee's books that cannot extend beyond the charged violation.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-20(a), who may initiate a complaint against a licensee?
choice_a: Only the licensee's broker
choice_b: Only a licensed attorney
choice_c: Only a party to the specific real estate transaction
choice_d: The commission itself, or any other person who files a complaint
explanation: §30-40-20(a) authorizes the commission to initiate a complaint on its own, or a complaint may be filed by another person, before the commission ascertains the facts and, if warranted, holds a hearing.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: What is the general limitations period for filing a disciplinary complaint under §30-40-20(a)?
choice_a: 2 years after the acts or omissions alleged in the complaint
choice_b: 1 year after the acts or omissions alleged
choice_c: 4 years after the acts or omissions alleged
choice_d: There is no limitations period
explanation: §30-40-20(a) bars disciplinary action on a complaint filed more than two years after the acts or omissions alleged in the complaint, except where the discovery rule for fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation applies.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Where a licensee is alleged to have engaged in fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation, §30-40-20(a) allows a complaint to be filed within what period?
choice_a: 2 years after the alleged unprofessional conduct occurred, with no discovery extension
choice_b: 2 years after the complainant discovered, or through reasonable diligence should have discovered, the alleged unprofessional conduct
choice_c: 6 months after discovery
choice_d: 10 years after discovery
explanation: §30-40-20(a) applies a discovery rule to fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation allegations: the two-year period runs from when the complainant discovered, or through reasonable diligence should have discovered, the alleged unprofessional conduct.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-20(a), what happens to the complaint filing deadline when material evidence is unavailable to the commission because of an ongoing criminal investigation or prosecution?
choice_a: The deadline is permanently waived
choice_b: The complaint is automatically dismissed
choice_c: The time limit is tolled during that period
choice_d: The deadline is shortened to 6 months
explanation: §30-40-20(a) provides that the time limits for filing a complaint are tolled during any period in which material evidence necessary for the commission's evaluation or use is unavailable due to an ongoing criminal investigation or prosecution.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: What form must a complaint against a licensee take under §30-40-20(b)?
choice_a: It may be made verbally to any commission member
choice_b: It must be notarized by a judge
choice_c: It must be filed anonymously
choice_d: It must be submitted in writing on a form prescribed by the commission, fully describing the alleged acts or omissions
explanation: §30-40-20(b) requires that all complaints be submitted in writing on a form prescribed by the commission and fully describe the acts or omissions constituting the alleged violation(s).

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: After the commission receives or initiates a complaint, §30-40-20(c) requires that the licensee be given a copy of the complaint and file an answer within how many days?
choice_a: 20 days
choice_b: 10 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: §30-40-20(c) requires the accused licensee to file an answer within 20 days of the date of service of the complaint, though an extension may be granted by the commission, its executive director, or an authorized representative.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-20(c), what is the consequence if a licensee fails to timely respond to a complaint?
choice_a: The complaint is automatically dismissed
choice_b: The failure may be considered an admission of the allegations
choice_c: The licensee's license is automatically revoked without a hearing
choice_d: No consequence attaches
explanation: §30-40-20(c) states that failure of the licensee to file a timely response may be considered an admission of the allegations contained in the complaint.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-20(d), what duty does a licensee have when the commission investigates a complaint?
choice_a: No duty; cooperation is voluntary
choice_b: A duty only if represented by counsel
choice_c: An affirmative duty to assist the commission or its authorized representative in the investigation
choice_d: A duty limited to producing a written statement only
explanation: §30-40-20(d) imposes an affirmative duty on any person licensed by the commission to assist the commission, or its authorized representative, in the conduct of its investigation.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: After reviewing a licensee's response and any investigation, if the commission determines probable cause exists under §30-40-20(e)-(f), what may it do?
choice_a: Immediately revoke the license with no further process
choice_b: Refer the matter exclusively to criminal court
choice_c: Take no further action
choice_d: Hold a hearing under §30-40-21, or dispose of the matter informally through a consent agreement or otherwise
explanation: §30-40-20(e)-(f) provides that once probable cause is found, the commission may hold a hearing consistent with §30-40-21, or resolve the matter informally, such as through a consent agreement.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-21(a), commission disciplinary hearings must be conducted in accordance with which law?
choice_a: §29A-5-1 et seq. of the WV Code (the State Administrative Procedures Act) and the commission's rules
choice_b: The West Virginia Rules of Civil Procedure only
choice_c: Federal Rules of Evidence exclusively
choice_d: Local circuit court rules
explanation: §30-40-21(a) requires hearings to be conducted in accordance with §29A-5-1 et seq. of the WV Code, the State Administrative Procedures Act, and the commission's own rules.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-21(b), a disciplinary hearing must be held at a time no earlier than how long after notice of hearing is given?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 30 days
choice_c: 15 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: §30-40-21(b) requires that hearings be held at a time and place the commission determines, but in no event less than 30 days after the notice of hearing is given.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-21(c), who has authority to administer oaths and examine a person under oath at a commission hearing?
choice_a: Only the executive director
choice_b: Only a licensed attorney representing the commission
choice_c: Any commission member
choice_d: Only a court reporter
explanation: §30-40-21(c) grants any commission member the authority to administer oaths and to examine any person under oath during a hearing.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: If, after a hearing, the commission determines a licensee violated the article or commission rules, §30-40-21(d) requires the resulting decision to contain what?
choice_a: Only a summary conclusion with no reasoning
choice_b: A recommendation to the Legislature only
choice_c: A public press release only
choice_d: Findings of fact, conclusions of law, and the specific disciplinary actions imposed
explanation: §30-40-21(d) requires a formal decision containing findings of fact, conclusions of law, and a specific list of the disciplinary actions imposed once a violation is found after hearing.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-21(e), if the commission elects to use an administrative law judge or hearing examiner, what must that person prepare at the hearing's conclusion?
choice_a: A proposed order containing findings of fact and conclusions of law, which the commission may accept, reject, or modify
choice_b: A binding final order the commission cannot alter
choice_c: A criminal referral
choice_d: A settlement check
explanation: §30-40-21(e) provides that an administrative law judge or hearing examiner, if used, prepares a proposed order with findings of fact and conclusions of law, which the commission may accept, reject, or modify, and may reserve the disciplinary determination for itself.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: A licensee adversely affected by a final commission disciplinary order is entitled to judicial review under which provision, per §30-40-21(f)?
choice_a: The WV Rules of Appellate Procedure only
choice_b: §29A-5-4 of the WV Code
choice_c: Direct appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court
choice_d: No judicial review is available
explanation: §30-40-21(f) entitles any person adversely affected by a final commission decision or order, made after hearing, to judicial review under §29A-5-4 of the WV Code.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: In addition to any other sanction, what may the commission require of a licensee under §30-40-21(g)?
choice_a: Payment of the commission's annual budget shortfall
choice_b: Mandatory relicensure exam regardless of outcome
choice_c: Payment of the costs of the disciplinary proceeding
choice_d: A public apology
explanation: §30-40-21(g) allows the commission, in addition to any other sanction imposed, to require a licensee to pay the costs of the disciplinary proceeding.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Which of the following is included among the sanctions the commission may impose on a licensee under §30-40-7(l)?
choice_a: Only license revocation, with no lesser sanctions available
choice_b: Only criminal referral
choice_c: Only a private warning letter with no formal record
choice_d: A range of sanctions including denial of license, administrative fine, probation, suspension, restitution, additional education, censure, or reprimand
explanation: §30-40-7(l) gives the commission a graduated menu of sanctions it may impose as appropriate, including denial of a license or renewal, administrative fines, probation, revocation, suspension, restitution, additional education, censure, downgrade of license, reprimand, or return of compensation.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-7(l), what is the maximum administrative fine the commission may impose per violation, per day?
choice_a: $1,000 per day
choice_b: $500 per day
choice_c: $2,500 per day
choice_d: $5,000 per day
explanation: §30-40-7(l) caps the commission's administrative fine authority at $1,000 per day per violation as one of the available disciplinary sanctions.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Per §30-40-9(c), how do administrative fines imposed under Article 40 differ from ordinary license fees in terms of where the money is deposited?
choice_a: Both go into the real estate license fund
choice_b: Administrative fines are deposited into the General Revenue Fund, while other fees go into the special "real estate license fund"
choice_c: Both go into the General Revenue Fund
choice_d: Fines go to the complainant directly
explanation: §30-40-9(c) directs administrative fines to the General Revenue Fund, unlike ordinary license fees and other moneys, which under §30-40-9(a) are deposited into the dedicated special revenue "real estate license fund."

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-19(d), every person licensed by the commission has what affirmative obligation?
choice_a: No obligation regarding other licensees' conduct
choice_b: A duty to represent other licensees in disciplinary hearings
choice_c: A duty to report, in a timely manner, any known or observed violation of the article or the commission's rules, orders, or final decisions
choice_d: A duty to personally investigate all complaints filed against colleagues
explanation: §30-40-19(d) imposes an affirmative duty on every licensee to report, in a timely manner, any known or observed violation of Article 40 or the commission's rules, orders, or final decisions.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-19(e), what happens to the licenses of associate brokers and salespersons affiliated with a broker whose license is revoked?
choice_a: Nothing; their licenses are unaffected
choice_b: Their licenses are automatically revoked permanently
choice_c: They must retake the licensing exam before continuing to work under any broker
choice_d: Their licenses are automatically suspended, though the commission will issue a free replacement license if the licensee obtains a new broker within the same license term
explanation: §30-40-19(e) provides that a broker's license revocation automatically suspends every affiliated associate broker's and salesperson's license, but the commission will issue a free replacement license to an affected licensee who secures a new broker and submits a proper application within the same license term.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-22(a), a first criminal violation of Article 40 by an individual is classified as what, and subject to what penalty?
choice_a: A misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not less than $1,000 nor more than $2,000, or confinement in jail up to 90 days, or both
choice_b: A felony, punishable by up to 5 years imprisonment
choice_c: A civil infraction with no fine
choice_d: An automatic license revocation only, with no fine or jail
explanation: §30-40-22(a) classifies a first violation of Article 40 or the commission's rules as a misdemeanor, punishable by a fine of not less than $1,000 nor more than $2,000, or confinement in jail up to 90 days, or both, in addition to any commission sanction.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-22(b), an individual convicted of a second or subsequent violation of Article 40 faces what penalty?
choice_a: The same penalty as a first offense
choice_b: A fine of not less than $2,000 nor more than $5,000, or confinement in jail up to one year, or both
choice_c: Automatic dismissal of all charges
choice_d: A civil fine only, capped at $500
explanation: §30-40-22(b) increases the penalty for a second or subsequent individual violation to a fine of not less than $2,000 nor more than $5,000, or confinement in jail for a term not to exceed one year, or both.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-22(c) and (d), how do criminal fines for a corporation, association, or partnership compare to those for an individual?
choice_a: Entities face no fines, only individuals do
choice_b: Entity fines are always lower than individual fines
choice_c: A first violation by an entity is fined $2,000-$5,000 (versus $1,000-$2,000 for an individual), and a second/subsequent entity violation is fined $5,000-$10,000
choice_d: Entity fines are capped at $1,000 regardless of violation count
explanation: §30-40-22(c)-(d) sets higher fine ranges for entities than for individuals: $2,000-$5,000 for a first violation by a corporation, association, or partnership, and $5,000-$10,000 for a second or subsequent violation.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-22(f), how is a continuing violation of Article 40 treated for penalty purposes?
choice_a: It is treated as a single offense regardless of duration
choice_b: Only the first day counts as an offense
choice_c: Continuing violations are automatically civil, not criminal
choice_d: Each day the violation continues constitutes a separate offense
explanation: §30-40-22(f) states that each day a violation of Article 40 continues constitutes a separate offense, allowing penalties to accumulate for ongoing noncompliance.

topic: General Powers and Duties of the Real Estate Commission
question: Under §30-40-22(g), a person who receives compensation for acts performed in violation of Article 40 is subject to what additional penalty, recoverable by the aggrieved person?
choice_a: A penalty of not less than the value of the compensation received nor more than three times that value
choice_b: No additional penalty beyond the misdemeanor fine
choice_c: A flat $10,000 civil penalty
choice_d: Forfeiture of their home
explanation: §30-40-22(g) subjects a person who receives compensation for acts performed in violation of the article to a penalty of not less than the value of the compensation received nor more than three times that value, which may be recovered by the person aggrieved by the violation.
